greek: Εἶπεν δὲ κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν λέγων

notes.text: Saying: the speech follows in 13:2.

greek: Ἁγίασόν μοι πᾶν πρωτότοκον πρωτογενὲς διανοῖγον πᾶσαν μήτραν ἐν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου ἕως κτήνους· ἐμοί ἐστιν.
hint: Every firstborn that opens the womb in Israel, human or animal, is to be consecrated to the lord.

notes.text: πρωτογενής, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's first-born, primeval, citing this verse, beside πρωτότοκον.
Opening every womb, the present participle of διανοίγω, for the Hebrew peṭer kol-reḥem; μήτρα, the womb, one translation, plain text.

greek: Εἶπεν δὲ Μωυσῆς πρὸς τὸν λαόν Μνημονεύετε τὴν ἡμέραν ταύτην, ἐν ᾗ ἐξήλθατε ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου ἐξ οἴκου δουλείας· ἐν γὰρ χειρὶ κραταιᾷ ἐξήγαγεν ὑμᾶς κύριος ἐντεῦθεν· καὶ οὐ βρωθήσεται ζύμη.
hint: Moses tells the people to remember the day they left Egypt, the house of slavery; nothing leavened is eaten.

notes.text: With a strong hand, for the Hebrew bĕḥōzeq yād.
Out of a house of servitude, for the Hebrew mibbêt ʿăbādîm.

greek: ἐν γὰρ τῇ σήμερον ὑμεῖς ἐκπορεύεσθε ἐν μηνὶ τῶν νέων.
hint: They go out today, in the month of new grain.

notes.text: In the month of the new things, νέος, for the Hebrew bĕḥōdeš hāʾābîb, in the month of the ears of grain.
The article, feminine, over the adverb σήμερον, to-day, Middle Liddell's one translation: the day understood.

reading: [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]], [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to the one to-day you [[you go out|you go out, you go forth, you march out|ἐκπορεύομαι]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to month [[of the young|of the young and youthful, of the new and fresh, of the new and strange|νέος]].

greek: καὶ ἔσται ἡνίκα ἐὰν εἰσαγάγῃ σε κύριος ὁ θεός σου εἰς τὴν γῆν τῶν Χαναναίων καὶ Χετταίων καὶ Ευαίων καὶ Γεργεσαίων καὶ Αμορραίων καὶ Φερεζαίων καὶ Ιεβουσαίων, ἣν ὤμοσεν τοῖς πατράσιν σου δοῦναί σοι, γῆν ῥέουσαν γάλα καὶ μέλι, καὶ ποιήσεις τὴν λατρείαν ταύτην ἐν τῷ μηνὶ τούτῳ.
hint: Once in the promised land of the seven peoples, flowing with milk and honey, they are to keep this rite.

notes.text: And of Girgashites: the Hebrew of this verse names five peoples, without the Girgashites and the Perizzites.
γάλα, milk, and μέλι, honey: Middle Liddell's one translation each, plain text.

greek: ἓξ ἡμέρας ἔδεσθε ἄζυμα, τῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ἑβδόμῃ ἑορτὴ κυρίου·
hint: Unleavened bread is eaten for six days, and the seventh day is a feast to the lord.

notes.text: Six days: the Hebrew has šibʿat yāmîm, seven days.

hint: Unleavened bread is eaten for the seven days; nothing leavened may be seen in all their territory.

notes.text: The seven days: the article over the numeral and its noun, printed once.
Nor will there be leaven to you, the dative of possession, for the Hebrew wĕlōʾ-yērāʾeh lĕkā śĕʾōr.

hint: A firstborn donkey is exchanged for a sheep or else redeemed, and every firstborn son is redeemed.

hint: Because the lord killed Egypt's firstborn when Pharaoh refused, firstborn males are offered and sons redeemed.

notes.text: Pharaoh hardened to send us away, σκληρύνω with the infinitive, for the Hebrew hiqšâ parʿōh lĕšallĕḥēnû.
